title: Diff two snapshots
description:
The inspector's snapshot panel compares two copies of the same memory range. Write `diffSnapshots(before, after, base, mergeGap)`, which returns the changed ranges as a list of `{ address, length }`:

- `before` and `after` are the bytes of the range starting at address `base`. If their sizes differ, only the common length is compared.
- A changed byte is one where `before[i] != after[i]`.
- Neighbouring changed bytes form one range. Two changed ranges separated by **at most `mergeGap` unchanged bytes** are merged into one range (which then includes the unchanged bytes between them), because a field that changed in two places reads better as one block.
- Ranges are returned in address order.

```
base 0x1000, before 00 00 00 00 00 00, after 00 11 00 22 00 00, mergeGap 0  ->  {0x1001,1} {0x1003,1}
                                                     the same with mergeGap 1  ->  {0x1001,3}
```
hints: Walk the bytes once. When you find a changed byte, extend it into a run of consecutive changed bytes.
Before adding a run, compare its start with the end of the last range: if the unchanged bytes between them number `mergeGap` or fewer, extend the last range to the end of the run instead.
lessonTitle: Capstone: A Memory Inspector with a Full Interface
